title: Divine Light and the Clouds of Mystery
english: They sent up smoke, which is consumed by the coming wrath, making coals. Coals were kindled from it. These coals signify, on the one hand, punishments, and on the other hand, the piercing, hot words of God that purify the thoughts of the soul.

Punishments are signified in: 'If your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him drink; for so doing you will heap coals of fire on his head' (Rom 12:20). And in: 'Coals of fire shall fall upon them, and you shall cast them down; they shall not help you' (Isa 51:6). The piercing word is shown in Isaiah: 'And he was sent among the seraphim.' Thus, prepared for the virtue of the soul, it warms and fires the thoughts to show them bright and splendid, but it will consume the deeds of sinners while purifying them; those not receiving this fire will be consumed by the eternal fire.

The phrase 'He inclined the heavens and came down' (Ps 18:10) follows the word concerning the economy and the descent. Since the Savior is said to dwell in the heavens, having become man, he changes his dwelling; for he became lowly and walked among men on earth. He dwells in the heavens not locally, nor does he descend transitively (for these are things pertaining to bodies), but according to the saying 'he dwells in the heavens.' For existing in the form of God, having taken the form of a servant, he descended, without any local change occurring to him.

And 'He rode upon the cherubim and flew' (Ps 18:10). The cherubim are understood as a voice for a multitude of knowledge; there is much knowledge there, but more ungraspable. One ascending from there flies through an elevated and ethereal intellect. It should not be thought that the name signifies the fullness of knowledge possessed by immortal animals. And God, having ascended upon these rational animals, flies through sharp intellect.

'He spread himself upon the wings of the winds' (Ps 134:1). If the saying is taken regarding the sensible winds, it means God, according to His providential word, mounting the wings of the winds, that is, by their lifting up as He Himself wills; for 'He draws out the winds from His treasuries' (Job 37:9). But if one were to take the winds as those blowing like judgments, lifting up wise men being moved by the spirit,

God rides upon the wings of these, which are higher and more lofty thoughts. There are winds of teaching, as the Apostle Paul says regarding heretics, speaking of every wind of teaching in the cunning of men, in craftiness toward the method of error. But not as false teachers are the winds upon whose wings the wandering spirits of the people ride; rather, God, riding upon the wings of every wind of true teaching, blows where He wills. And this is to be spread upon the wings of winds.

Previously and truly, the God who dwells is unapproachable light, the Son who is true light, and the Holy Spirit who is the possession of knowledge and wisdom, just as of this light it is said, 'And the light is with Him' (John 1:14). Secondly, by reason of the incomprehensibility concerning His essence, it is said that His hiddenness is called darkness. For that which is indistinct and incomprehensible because of the depth of the matter is called darkness. In this way, it is said that He perceives a parable and a dark speech; and God, uncovering the deeps out of darkness, makes manifest and clear those things hidden under indistinctness and difficulty of comprehension.

His tabernacle is around Him. Just as he who is contained under a tabernacle cannot be seen unless he has entered into it, so also the God surrounded by indistinctness and difficulty of comprehension cannot be seen unless one has entered into the interior of the covering of that difficulty. Immediately, regarding Moses, it is said how he entered into the cloud where God was (Exodus 19:9). For having understood the thought, the creation, and the providence concerning God, he knew that God is contained by these; thus, having slightly passed through this tabernacle concerning Him, he might behold from the image (which is not the image) the one according to the image, and from the creation and providence, the Creator and Provider.

In many places of the Scripture, we find clouds being carried allegorically. For he who said 'the vineyard of Israel,' speaking of clouds receiving commands not to rain upon it, we find no others but the prophets. It is not only with them that 'Thus says the Lord' and 'The word of the Lord came to me' are found; until these clouds, the truth shines. For these clouds are souls.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Springs of Water and the Foundations of the World
english: Flowing as a rain of spiritual words, they belong to the air, not the earth; for having detached themselves from earthly things and no longer thinking of them, they are lifted up and exalted by their own virtue and by the active spirit of the air.

The water within them, before having attained clarity and manifestation through Jesus, is said to be a dark thing, being difficult for the many to see. But when God has spoken in the Son at the end of days, the law and the prophets shall be fulfilled: they shall come together before him in a bright shining (that is to say, his illumination), visible clouds and distinct, because of the presence of what was pre-proclaimed by them (Ps 17:13b–15).

Since no apology remains for those sinning, coming out of dark clouds into light through clarity, there immediately follows the bright shining of the clouds with hail and coals of fire. This is signified by the punishments through the pre-proclamations and having attained the manifestation of what was prophesied concerning Christ.

God immediately thunders from heaven, either through the loud voice of the words being fulfilled by Jesus, or by casting the highest words of theology concerning the only-begotten Son into each mind, not only having cried out this: 'This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased,' but also the Most High gives a voice to those who discourse highly concerning Christ, who did not reveal his own Son to them in flesh, but the Father in heaven revealed his own Son.

Just as for those prepared in mind for the vision of God and the hearing of the Word, the Lord thunders from heaven and the Most High gives his voice, so that, being lifted up by the thunder coming from heaven, they may fall away from earthly things and fly toward heaven, bearing the image of the heavenly, and may receive the high things of the thoughts being given by the Most High; but to those who are of contrary disposition, the Lord sends arrows sufficient to throw into confusion those who previously were of one mind concerning evil.
But now the arrows say the words pre-proclaiming the punishments; for the threats are sufficient to disturb and agitate the soul, and he shall clarify even the threats spoken in enigmas...

He will light up like lightning, and will throw into confusion those scattered by the aforementioned arrows. For those being scattered cast off their agreement toward evil, having become in turmoil and confusion.

[Ps 17:16a] When all the aforementioned things have happened, the springs of the waters will be seen. And if someone says that the springs of the waters are those sown among us concerning God and good thoughts, he will say that these will be seen when the ignorance and malice lying upon the soul are withdrawn. For these, having been removed, will not hide the springs of good things in us. But if someone says that every God-breathed scripture, though spiritual, is veiled by ambiguity, [he says] that the springs will be seen; stand firm! For if we turn now to the Lord, the veil of ignorance and ambiguity will be removed, and the springs of the waters lying within will be seen, so that it is easy to draw from each one, according to [Ps 36:9] 'Draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.' For this water of gladness is a part of the being of the springs of salvation, which were granted to the discerning one, and now he sees God, according to [Ps 34:8] 'Bless the Lord in the churches, O Israel, from the springs.'

[Ps 17:16bc] He acts through the building up of the inhabited world and says, and thinks of certain foundations; he is not speaking of the sins and dispositions of yours when he speaks of the foundations of the inhabited world. For if he scatters the wicked with his arrows and throws them into confusion, by the flashing of his lightning, making the hidden things of men become manifest, by the lighting of God of the secrets of darkness and by making manifest the foundations of the inhabited world, he will uncover the deep things from darkness from the rebuke of the inhabited world by him over all. And if someone says that the foundations of the inhabited world are the divine men, because of the goodness of life and the narrowness of virtue upon which those living according to Christ are built, the uncovering of these foundations too will happen, through the occurrence of a rebuke. For the uncovering and revealing of these foundations will not happen without the punishment of these [sinners].
[Ps 17:16d] God does not delay the punishments for those sinning. For if this were to happen, all would be utterly lost. But by goodness...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Righteousness of God's Judgments
english: Because of great human-lovingness, even though a multitude of sins occurs constantly, He does not bring down wrath for every single day. This is what it means for Him to breathe His own spirit of wrath, because He pre-announces the punishments of wrath: 'For I will discipline them in the wrath of their affliction' (Ps 17:17).

Out of many waters—meaning the turbulent and salty matters of life, called a sea tropically, which are the poured-out and disordered opposing powers—He stands against them; and even if the doctrines of ungodliness are many, they are not able to quench love. God delivers from powerful enemies the invisible ones, as is said, and perhaps also those in high positions and those intending to deceive through pseudonymous knowledge, who are terrible in their sophistry.

No one is without their own private thoughts, and those who are dissatisfied with Providence also bring up impiety regarding others, calling them powerful enemies, and that they might be rescued from those who hate them, and that they might be strengthened above them, which is worthy, while the haters are in vain. For no one, being hated for something trivial, will have the boldness to speak this prayer to God, but rather if he is hated by sinners for Christ and for the upright life, those who loathe godliness, for they consider the conduct of the righteous to be a reproach to their own way of life.

Indeed, those who hate the righteous most vehemently attack then, when a time of affliction is present. For, being ignorant of the judgment of Providence, they suppose that the righteous is being afflicted through sin for no other reason, like those conversing with Job. For when God had subjected him to afflictions, so that he might be shown to be righteous, they said that this man had fallen into these things because of impiety and sin; but even against the one stumbling, all the predatory demons and the devil are strong, as they now think sin to be an evil.

For in the day of affliction, whoever takes refuge toward God, He becomes his support (Ps 17:19), meaning, supporting him so that he might not be shaken and fall. And concerning the perfection of the soul, those who accept the ascent and the brightening of it say marvelously: 'Who is she that ascends...'

Has she been whitened, leaning upon her brother? For the Lord becomes a support for someone, leading him out of the narrowness of afflictions, giving him breadth according to 'In affliction he enlarged me' (Ps 17:20a). But one is enlarged in affliction not by becoming outside of the affliction entirely, but by being courageously and piously stretched toward it.

He will rescue me from my strong enemies and from those hating me (Ps 17:20b–21), since they possess no power at all, for all His wills were doing me. Truly, the boldness of the pure and perfect is such that he condemns nothing of himself, even the shortest thing; therefore, those who wish to speak this psalm in the presence of the Savior, and who apply this word to Him, find Him having been tested in all things according to likeness, without sin. He speaks of righteousness as the general virtue of practice, and of cleanness of hands as the practical actions becoming pure and unstained by being fulfilled from the best of ways; for often hands are said to be upon the practical powers.

And he does not say these things arrogantly, as some are, but having placed the cause of the successes upon God. He who walks in His commandments keeps the ways of the Lord, and he who has correctly grasped the doctrines of truth does not act impiously toward his own God, conceiving blamelessly concerning God, speaking holily concerning Christ, remembering piously concerning the Holy Spirit, and glorifying in the proper manner concerning the other doctrines.

For even if His judgments are unsearchable and seem like an abyss because of the incomprehensible, it is not possible for those having them not to be displeased with Providence, nor to act impiously toward the one who provides. For even if we do not grasp, but having resolved that these things are fulfilled by God's judgment, we are well-pleased with them. And the very name 'Judgment' signifies the rectitude of the administration; for it contains and is heard to be that which has happened according to righteousness, as opposed to judgments of the unrighteous and the perverted which are performed apart from the right. Because of this, he says, a perverted judgment will come forth. 'I hold fast to the rights of God,' he says (Ps 17:23b).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
